    AI Overview
    Trump Accounts
    are tax-advantaged investment accounts for children under 18, launched via the One Big Beautiful Bill Act of 2025. They feature a $1,000 federal seed deposit for children born 2025–2028 and allow up to $5,000 in annual contributions, going live in July 2026. Parents can enroll using IRS Form 4547. 
    Key Features and Rules 
    • Eligibility: U.S. citizens under 18 with a valid Social Security number.
    • Seed Money: Children born between January 1, 2025, and December 31, 2028, receive a $1,000 contribution from the U.S. Treasury.
    • Contributions: Up to $5,000 can be contributed annually (tax-deferred) per child.
    • Employer Matching:
      Employers can contribute up to $2,500 per year, which counts toward the $5,000 total limit.
    • Investment: Funds are invested in, for example, S&P 500 index-tracking ETFs or mutual funds.
    • Withdrawals: The account functions like a traditional IRA, with potential penalties for early withdrawals before age 18, though funds can be used for specific education or housing expenses. 
    How to Open 
    • Parents can initiate the process by filing IRS Form 4547 when filing taxes, with the account formally going live on July 4, 2026, or July 5, 2026, according to various reports.
    • The accounts are managed as custodial accounts until the child reaches age 18.

    What is a Trump account?

    AI Overview
    A Trump Account is a tax-advantaged individual retirement savings account for children under 18, established by the
    One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA). It aims to build long-term financial security with a $1,000 federal contribution pilot program for eligible U.S. citizen children born between Jan. 1, 2025, and Dec. 31, 2028, according to the IRS and trumpaccounts.gov. 
    Key Features of Trump Accounts: 
    • Eligibility: Children must be U.S. citizens under age 18 with a valid Social Security number.
    • Funding: Parents, guardians, and employers can contribute. The maximum annual contribution is generally
      per child, which will be indexed for inflation starting in 2028.
    • Employer Match: Employers can contribute up to
      per year, which is tax-free to the employee, as described in this Fidelity article.
    • Pilot Program: Children born between 2025 and 2028 may receive a $1,000 contribution from the U.S. Treasury, as shown on the Trump Accounts website.
    • Withdrawals: Money is designed for long-term growth and generally cannot be withdrawn until age 18. Early withdrawals before age
      may incur a
      penalty, though exceptions exist for education, first-time home purchases, or starting a business, says The American Action Forum.
    • Opening an Account: Parents can initiate the process by filing Form 4547 with their taxes, according to the IRS. 
    The initiative is designed to encourage early, long-term investments in equities to build wealth for the next generation, according to the U.S. Department of the Treasury.

      You may have seen a question about a “Trump Account” on your taxes and wonder what it’s all about? Well, it’s similar to an IRA, but for kids under 18. I’m a little disappointed they didn’t make it a Roth account, because you kind of get a “worst of both worlds” on the tax break. You pay tax on your income up front, then on any growth instead of getting the lower long term capital gains rate, your kid pays income tax again upon withdrawal. There are certainly scenarios where you would end up with more money in a regular old taxable account. That said, you do get the normal tax-advantaged account benefit of “deferred taxes”. That means any dividends or gains along the way compound right inside of the account with any tax drag. There’s also a cool opportunity for a “backdoor Roth” strategy.
